body:
## Problem

Two UI papercuts in the Vista blocks kit:

1. **The split divider was not the drag target.** `ResizableSplit` rendered a 6px handle track containing a separate 1px `<span>` line. Visually that reads as two things — a line plus an invisible gutter around it — and the gutter widened every grid template by 6px per split.
2. **Wasted space above the treemap canvas** in the PR viewer's `treemap="above"` placement. The treemap's fill chain never actually stretched: `canvasFill` set `height: auto`, `rootFill` inherited the root's `0.6rem` flex gap, and `stageFill`'s basis resolved against content. The result was a dead strip between the controls row and the tiles.

## Goal

The divider *is* the handle — one 1px line, directly draggable, React Aria owning the a11y semantics. The treemap fills its pane with no dead space.

## Decisions

- **Each seam draws exactly one hairline.** The file rail, the diff pane, and the filled treemap canvas each carried their own 1px frame, so a split seam stacked three lines (pane border + separator + pane border) and doubled rounded corners where they met. The surrounding surface now owns the edges: those three drop their frames and the separator is the only line. The viewer's own border still frames the whole block.
- **Hit area via an overlaid `::after`, not transparent borders.** The first attempt used `borderInline: '4px solid transparent'` + negative margin. StyleX does not emit the `borderInline` shorthand, so only the margin landed — no grab tolerance, and the divider sat 4px off its track. An absolutely positioned `::after` inset `-4px` widens the pointer target with no layout cost.

- **`useSeparator` for role/orientation only.** React Aria Components has no resizable-panel primitive (that's `react-resizable-panels`, a dependency we don't want). `useSeparator` from bare `react-aria` gives `role="separator"` + orientation; the window-splitter value props (`aria-valuemin/max/now`, `aria-controls`) stay explicit because `filterDOMProps` strips them. `useMove`/`useHover`/`useFocusRing` keep owning drag and keyboard, unchanged.
- **Hit area via transparent borders, not a wrapper element.** `borderInline: 4px solid transparent` + `marginInline: -4px` + `backgroundClip: padding-box` widens the pointer target over both panes while the painted divider stays 1px and the grid track stays 1px. No extra DOM, no layout shift.
- **`react-aria` (bare) not a new dep.** Already imported by this same file and by `service-hub/console-resize.tsx`; resolved transitively via `react-aria-components`. No manifest change.

## Verification

Storybook snapshot of this branch: **https://vista-ui-2026-09.scratch.schickling.dev**

- [Resizable Split](https://vista-ui-2026-09.scratch.schickling.dev/?path=/story/vista-blocks-layout-resizable-split--default) — drag the line itself; grab tolerance extends ~4px each side.
- [PullRequestViewer](https://vista-ui-2026-09.scratch.schickling.dev/?path=/story/vista-blocks-code-pullrequestviewer--default) — treemap banner, no gap above the tiles.

Measured in a live browser (`playwright-cli`, `document.getBoundingClientRect`):

```
                        before            after
separator box           6 x 414 px        1 x 414 px
separator background    transparent       rgba(255,255,255,0.14)   (the line moved onto the separator itself)
role / orientation      manual attrs      separator | vertical  (useSeparator)
treemap figure 176px    controls 29 + stage 140  → 7px dead      controls 29 + stage 147, canvas 147, tiles 145  → 0
```

Checks:

```
vitest run          15 files / 126 tests passed
tsc -p tsconfig     clean
check:quick         passed (ts:check, lint, genie, lockfile)
```

`check:all` had one red lane, `test:crosstask:rust-nomad-client`, alongside a bare `execute command ... (failed)` after ~26 min of contended Rust builds. Re-run standalone on this exact tree it is green in 256s:

```
✓ Running test:crosstask:rust-nomad-client in 256s
```

This diff touches three `.tsx` files in `flakes/vista/blocks` and nothing Rust or crosstask, so the lane failure is contention/flake, not this change.

## Complexity

No new complexity — net −7 lines, one DOM node removed per split, one dependency import added from a package already in the closure.

## Concerns

- The transparent-border hit area is a CSS trick. It is self-contained in two style objects and commented, but a future change to `boxSizing` or `backgroundClip` on `separator` would silently break either the 1px look or the grab tolerance. The story exercises the drag; it does not assert the hit-area width.
- `useSeparator` only contributes `role` + `aria-orientation` here. That is genuinely thin, and the explicit `aria-orientation` on the element is belt-and-braces (RA omits it for the horizontal default, which the existing test asserts on). Kept explicit so the rendered contract does not depend on RA's defaulting.

## Friction & bottlenecks

- The dev3 Devnet edge is down: `devnet doctor` reports `registryWritable: false`, `observationState: missing`, `transportProbe` fails TLS (`curl (35)`), and both live sessions sit `unrealized`. So `devnet publish` cannot hand out a `*.dev3.devnet.schickling.dev` URL at all right now — the existing `service-hub` route is equally dead. Worked around with a `deploy-scratch` static Storybook build. Not filed; reporting here first in case this is known/expected on dev3.
- `devnet up` with a bare `node …` argv silently created a session that never appeared in `devnet list`/`status`; only the `bash -lc … corepack pnpm exec …` shape (copied from the existing service-hub session) registered. Two dead sessions were created before that landed.

## Follow-ups

- None blocking. If the hit-area tolerance is worth locking down, a Playwright assertion on `elementFromPoint` at ±4px would do it.

## References

Follows the Vista pull-request block work on this branch (#2879 lineage — `05841cc`, `f4745a8`).

commits.messageBody:
ResizableSplit drops the 6px handle track + inner line span. The 1px
divider is the resize target (useSeparator owns role/orientation);
transparent 4px borders + negative margins keep it grabbable without
layout cost. Treemap fill chain (figure grid, root gap 0, stage 0%
basis, canvas 100%) removes the dead space above the canvas in the
PR viewer above-placement.
commits.messageHeadline: feat(vista): border-draggable split divider, treemap fills pane

pane border). The surrounding surface owns the edges now: panes and the

The grab tolerance also never applied — StyleX does not emit the
`borderInline` shorthand, so the transparent 4px borders were absent and
only the negative margin landed, offsetting the divider. Replaced with an
overlaid ::after, which widens the pointer target without touching
layout.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(vista): one hairline per seam, and a hit area that actually applies
